description:
Goal
A polymorphic (type-variable-bearing) activation must not survive as a ground backend executable. Eliminate the phantom (a0,a0) activation that blocks Enum.with_index native lowering.

Discovered while landing fz-hwn.22 (boxed-callable value shape = pure layout). With fz-hwn.22 in place, the Enum.with_index mapper repro clears the continuation-capture bug and then fails native lowering with:
  native lowering invariant failed: backend value ValueId(0) in executable ExecutableKey { activation: ActivationKey { root: RootId(0), function: FunctionId(164), input: [Ty(27), Ty(27)] }, need: Value } must be runtime-materializable
where Ty(27) is the type variable a0 -- FunctionId(164) is activated polymorphically at [a0, a0].

Why
This is the same class of defect first surfaced in fz-hwn.21: the mapper / Enum-internal functions thread through generic recursive code (with_index_list/3 etc.) and pick up phantom polymorphic surfaces/activations like (a0,a0) and (a0,a1). fz-hwn.21 GROUNDED the dispatch SURFACES (so no phantom boundaries publish), but the phantom polymorphic ACTIVATION itself still gets monomorphized into a backend executable whose body cannot materialize a runtime value (a type variable has no value-lane repr). A polymorphic activation is an inference-phase artifact; it must be grounded or pruned before it becomes a backend executable. Type variables must never reach representation (see project_fz_hwn_grounding_arc, feedback_types_is_the_calculator).

Required work
- Identify where FunctionId(164)[a0,a0] (and siblings) are created as backend executables and why the grounding from fz-hwn.21 does not eliminate the phantom ACTIVATION (only the surfaces).
- Ground or prune polymorphic activations so no type-variable-bearing activation reaches the backend; fix in the right place (activation keying / semantic closure), not by special-casing Enum.
- Re-enable compiler2_interp_runs_enum_with_index_mapper_from_backend_artifacts (expects ["a!","b!"]) and make it pass.

Checks
- target/debug/fz2 interp on the with_index repro completes and dbg prints ["a!", "b!"].
- No backend executable has a type-variable-bearing activation input.
- Full lib + fixture matrix green, no warnings.

Repro: target/debug/fz2 interp /tmp/fz2-enum-with-index.fz (fn main do dbg(Enum.with_index(["a","b"], fn (x,_index) -> x <> "!" end)) end).
title: Phantom polymorphic activation reaches the backend (FunctionId[a0,a0] not runtime-materializable)
